newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call ends quiet, market awaits repo results.
newsitem.headline: Indian call ends quiet, market awaits repo results.

text.p: Indian call money ended Thursday at 6.0-6.25 percent against opening quotes of 7.0-7.5 percent while prices of government securities were up in light trade, dealers said.
Trades in call money were on a low key as most banks had covered their positions ahead of the reporting Friday.
Banks in India report their positions to the central bank on alternate Fridays.
"Call money opened slightly down from yesterday's 7.25-7.5 percent and kept drifting down," said a dealer. "Today's repo auction will determine how call money opens on Saturday."
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) held a repo auction earlier in the afternoon and results are due later today.
At its last auction the RBI mopped up 37.5 billion rupees. This is reversed on Friday.
Dealers said call money rates will be determined by the net flows after today's auction and Friday's repurchase by the RBI.
Prices of government securities were firm in cautious trade as market players awaited the results of the auction.
"If funds flow back and call money comes down, then trade in securities will pick up," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
Trade on Friday was mainly in stocks with tenures up to 2004, he said.

Among active stocks, the 10.85 percent 2001 traded at 100.75 rupees against its previous close of 100.71, the 13.85 percent 2001 rose to 109.54 from 109.45 while the 11 percent 2002 improved to 100.40 from 100.20, dealers said.
The 12.59 percent 2004 traded between 105.76 and 105.82 against 105.69.
